verdict.reasoning: Patient states: 'I just got a terrible headache since mid-day. Um on the left side.' and later describes it as 'throbbing, um on that left side.'

Patient says: 'I noticed some zig-zag lines in my vision a few minutes before the headache started.' and 'My vision blurred.' indicating a visual aura and transient blurred vision preceding the headache.

Patient: 'it's worse when I move... if I lean forward, or like move my head or neck, yeah, headache gets worse.' Also: 'wearing sunglasses right now. It's just, you know, the light's really hurting my eyes.' and 'I just feel like I need to vomit.' 'I vomited twice.' This supports movement-related worsening, photophobia, and nausea/vomiting x2.

Fever: Patient: 'Um, no I don't feel feverish.' Rash: 'No, I haven't noticed anything like that.' Speech: 'Have you noticed any problems with your speech...?' Patient: 'No.' Limb weakness/numbness: 'Any problems with your arms and legs?...' Patient: 'No.' Balance: 'Any difficulty with balance, your balance or coordination?' Patient: 'No.' Head trauma: 'Have you had a fall recently, or been knocked on the head?' Patient: 'No.' Shortness of breath: doctor asks about breathing and patient gives no concern; doctor concludes she is otherwise OK. Thus absence of these symptoms is documented.

Patient: 'I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago.' Duration: 'How long did it last for?' Patient: 'Couple of days.' Also: 'I'm not really prone to them, no.' supports that otherwise headaches are rare.

Patient repeatedly expresses concern: 'I've read, you know if your headache gets worse if you move, it could be a sign of brain cancer.' and 'I was so worried that I had cancer.' and family history of a brain tumor. This supports concern about a brain tumor.

When asked: 'Do you have any other medical history I should be aware of?' Patient: 'No, nothing.' This supports no reported past medical history (beyond what is later detailed as family history and current medication).
Patient: 'Um I take the pill, Microgynon.' Doctor: 'And how long have you been on that for?' Patient: 'three months.' and confirms it's for contraception.
Patient: 'My mum, my mum has, has migraines.' and later: 'My mom has an underactive thyroid as well.' This supports maternal migraines and hypothyroidism.
Patient: 'I work in the fashion industry.' and 'Yeah it's really stressful, actually.' plus 'I live on my own.' supports employment in fashion, high stress, and living alone.

Exercise: Doctor: 'Do you do much in the way of exercise?' Patient: 'No.' Smoking and alcohol: Doctor: 'Do you smoke at all? and do you drink much in the way of alcohol?' Patient: 'No. No.' This supports no exercise routine, non-smoker, and no alcohol use.

Doctor: 'I wonder whether you may, uh may have a migraine, uh migraine type headache. Uh it sounds very classical of that... the headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, um sensitivity to bright lights.' Aura is described earlier (zig-zag lines, blurred vision), there are no focal neurological signs per negative neuro ROS. Thus 'migraine with aura, recurrent with typical features and no focal neurological signs' matches the consultation.

Patient shows marked worry: 'I'm just really worried... could be a sign of brain cancer.' 'My friend's mum... died of a brain tumor. So, it's really concerning me actually.' 'What if it is a brain tumour? What's gonna happen with my future and my career?' This supports health anxiety focused on intracranial malignancy.

Doctor: 'to treat your headaches today, some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, think about Paracetamol, or even Co-codamol. Um, and some anti-inflammatories, such as Ibuprofen and Naproxen.' This matches the stated plan.
Doctor: 'I think keeping a headache diary would be quite important, uh to see exactly what's triggering these headaches.'

Doctor: 'if your headaches were to become more persistent, then we could maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place, something prophylactic medicines. then we could have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps.' This supports prophylactic options and review next week.

Doctor: 'if your symptoms aren't getting better next two three days, or indeed they're getting worse. I'd like you to come back and see me... So if your headache's getting worse, not responding to medications Or your um neck pain is getting worse, or you develop any weakness in your arms and legs, or your vision, then I want you to come back and see me straight away.' This matches safety-net advice described.

Doctor explicitly reassures: 'I'm reassured that you don't have anything more serious, such as meningitis, or indeed Brain cancer, I know that was a big worry of yours initially.' and patient responds with relief. This constitutes reassurance about low likelihood of brain tumor.
